newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-ECCLESTONE SAYS HE WON'T BROKER DEAL FOR HILL.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ECCLESTONE SAYS HE WON'T BROKER DEAL FOR HILL.

text.p: Formula One supremo Bernie Ecclestone said on Sunday he was sure Damon Hill would join a top Formula One team next season, but he ruled out using his considerable influence to broker a deal for the British driver.
"Damon needs to be in a car where he can defend his title and I'm sure that's what will happen," the Formula One Constructors' Association president told BBC television.
"He deserves to be in a top team," he said. "Damon is a much better driver now. He has changed completely this season."
Hill was dropped from the successful Williams team last week, just when he moved to within touching distance of his first world drivers' championship title.
He was replaced by German driver Heinz-Harald Frentzen, currently with the Swiss team Sauber.

Hill spun out of the Italian Grand Prix at Monza on Sunday but still takes a 13-point lead over Williams team mate Jacques Villeneuve of Canada into the penultimate race of the season at Estoril in Portugal in two weeks' time.
Ecclestone, widely regarded as the most powerful man in Grand Prix racing, said he was puzzled by the decision of Williams team boss Frank Williams to drop the British driver.

"If (Hill) could have carried the number one for Williams next season, it would have been a good thing for Frank, but it seems Frank doesn't like world champions in his team. He makes world champions but then gets rid of them.
"He feels Frentzen is a better prospect long term than Hill," Ecclestone added. "He may well be right -- only time will tell -- but I don't think that's true."
Hill has been linked with the Jordan, McLaren and Benneton teams for next year.
